candidates.title: Commission and lock a compact industrial robot-axis shock absorber
candidates.objective: With the representative axis isolated, physically seat a hex bit and loosen—but do not extract—the captive setscrew in the moving numbered collar; withdraw the bit, rotate the collar within its published 180° adjustment, reacquire the relocated socket, relock the setting, physically operate a guarded cycle control, and iteratively obtain two repeatable carriage stops without bottoming, overload, excessive rebound, or setting drift.
skills: hex-bit withdrawal and socket reacquisition after collar motion
controlled fine rotation of a small numbered collar
bimanual counterholding without invented torsional spring load
iterative adjustment from observed dynamic response
candidates.success_conditions: Use a rigid PhysX carriage with physically simulated drive, contact, axial return spring, 12.0 mm damper stroke, and external hard stop. Test energy must be at least 0.85 J—5% of the published 17.0 Nm/cycle maximum—and impact velocity must remain within 0.3–3.30 m/s and the conservative usable-setting bound read from the ECO OEM Small Series chart. The robot must loosen the captive setscrew, withdraw the bit, turn the collar, reacquire the moved socket, relock it, and physically initiate each test. Success requires two consecutive measured stops without exceeding stroke, striking the hard stop, exceeding published reaction/propelling limits, excessive rebound, or post-lock collar drift. Partial credit covers safe engagement, unlocking, adjustment, reacquisition, and locking. Zero score applies to energized adjustment, dropped tools, thread damage, unsafe collision, hard-stop impact, direct task-object pose/velocity/damping writes, collision suppression, welding, teleportation, or hidden demo-stage success flags.
candidates.industrial_value: The AZ-100 robot manual identifies shock-absorber adjustment as robot-axis maintenance. The Enidine catalog independently documents a compact adjustable hydraulic shock absorber, its geometry, operating limits, adjustment collar, and setscrew locking. The representative fixture therefore models an industrial commissioning operation without claiming that the Enidine unit is interchangeable with the AZ-100 component or that an unpublished manufacturer force curve is reproduced.
candidates.dexterity: The task combines small-socket tool alignment, controlled torque, counterholding, collar regrasping, mandatory tool withdrawal and reacquisition after the socket moves, retention of a fine setting during relocking, and feedback-driven dynamic commissioning. Its outcome depends on measured stopping behavior rather than knob rotation alone.

candidates.asset_plan: Author a full-scale representative non-button ECO OEM .35M-form fixture using 12.0 mm stroke, M16×1.5 housing thread, D=4.0 mm piston rod diameter, G=11.2 mm adjustment-knob diameter, H=14.5 mm axial knob length, F=87.4 mm indicated housing portion, and A=100.6 mm overall envelope. Do not mix optional-button A1/E1 dimensions into this version. Preserve the moving 180° collar and a captive contact-bearing setscrew. An independently authored M3×3 DIN 916-style screw with 0.5 mm pitch and 1.5 mm socket may be disclosed as a representative prototype choice, not an Enidine specification. Use a guarded rigid carriage near 1 J and 0.5 m/s, then validate at 240 Hz: energy balance, stroke, hard-stop contact, reaction and propelling loads, rebound, low/high-setting controls, lock retention, socket contact, parameter sensitivity, and clean reset. The robot must physically press the cycle control; no episode-time teleportation, welding, or direct state completion is allowed.
candidates.risk: The catalog does not publish collar torque, the original setscrew dimensions, friction, or a force-versus-setting calibration. These must remain disclosed bounded assumptions and pass component sensitivity, contact, stability, and witness-torque tests before YAM integration. The source chart must be conservatively digitized for the chosen velocity, and the representative damping law must not be described as manufacturer calibrated. The phase-15 reach result is only an IK planning lead, not grasp, collision, contact, or simulation validation.

candidates.title: Safely replace and rebalance a spring-balancer-supported industrial tool
candidates.objective: Physically index and proof-check an EWA-15 drum lock, support and remove the suspended tool, attach a replacement within the rated mass range, adjust spring preload through the worm while reading the gauge, and release the lock under control until the tool remains balanced.
skills: controlled release under stored spring energy
candidates.success_conditions: The pin must physically enter a drum slot and resist a proof motion before tool removal. The replacement must remain supported, be within 9–15 kg, and be attached before unlocking. After preload adjustment and controlled release, it must remain hands-off without abrupt rise, drop, snap-back, or overtravel. Unsafe unlocked removal, tool drop, direct state writes, welded retention, or teleportation scores zero.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer’s tool-replacement procedure explicitly requires drum locking, secure-lock checking, load support, preload adjustment, attachment before release, and final balance checking.
candidates.dexterity: The operation combines indexed locking, proof loading, heavy suspended-load stabilization, hook manipulation, wrench engagement, gauge feedback, and release of stored spring energy.

candidates.asset_plan: A mechanically faithful representative fixture would require a physical drum, indexed slot lock, pull/turn pin, worm-driven preload mechanism, readable gauge, retaining hook, 1.3 m payout constraint, and a 9–15 kg replacement load. Component tests must cover false seating, proof-load retention, hook retention, payout, preload direction, hands-off balance, unsafe release, overload, and reset repeatability.
candidates.risk: The acquired manual establishes operation and capacity but does not dimension the lock pin, drum slots, worm, gauge, hook, or housing. The required payload and stored-energy behavior also remain unverified for the pinned YAM robot and runtime.
missing_evidence: Dimensioned lock-pin, drum-slot, worm, gauge, hook, and housing geometry

Pinned-YAM reach, grip-force, and payload validation for a 9–15 kg suspended load
Validated spring, payout, hook-retention, and unsafe-release physics

candidates.title: Track and tension an industrial robot timing belt
candidates.objective: With power isolated, physically adjust the two-sided belt-tracking mechanism in small increments, manually traverse the axis after each correction, observe lateral belt motion, and iteratively center the belt without slack or overtension.
candidates.success_conditions: The robot must physically operate both adjusters and manually traverse the axis after each correction. Success requires centered belt travel over repeated full traversals plus a sourced model-specific tension criterion. Powered adjustment, direct belt-state writes, invisible centering constraints, flange climbing, slack, overtension, or damage scores zero.
candidates.industrial_value: The robot manufacturer identifies belt tracking and tensioning as maintenance operations and states that incorrect adjustment can reduce performance and cause premature belt failure.
candidates.dexterity: The task alternates paired fine adjustment, manual traversal, observation of belt creep, and asymmetric correction, but credible difficulty depends on validated belt and pulley contact physics.

candidates.asset_plan: Do not construct this candidate without an already validated closed-loop belt/contact example for Isaac Sim 6.1. A faithful fixture also needs sourced belt profile, pulley and flange dimensions, span, adjuster geometry, carriage geometry, and a numeric tension criterion. Validation must cover lateral tracking, flange climbing, slack, overtension, manual traversal, and repeatability.
candidates.risk: This is a deformable or highly contact-sensitive closed-loop belt problem. The acquired evidence supplies the procedure but neither a validated compatible solver example nor sufficient model-specific geometry and tension data.
missing_evidence: Validated belt/contact example compatible with the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1 Arena/YAM runtime
Dimensioned belt, pulley, flange, span, adjuster, and carriage geometry
Model-specific numeric tension or deflection criterion
Physics validation that asymmetric adjustment produces credible lateral tracking

selection_reason: This is the only candidate with sufficient primary geometry, operating limits, adjustment range, retention mechanism, industrial robot-maintenance relevance, and a plausible rigid-PhysX construction path in the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1/YAM runtime. It requires more than generic knob rotation or fastener tightening: the moving socket forces physical bit withdrawal and reacquisition, the collar setting must be retained while locking, and success depends on repeated measured impact behavior. Selection is for factual/feasibility preflight; the existing novelty critic’s unresolved six-suite and catalog-uncertainty findings must still be closed before freezing a construction contract.
